units.source: Exporting static HTML for web publishing
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing

units.source: As described in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Sharing__TRILIUM_PH_1__, Trilium can act as a public server in which the shared notes are displayed in read-only mode. While this can work in most cases, it's generally not meant for high-traffic websites and since it's running on a Node.js server it can be potentially exploited.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing

units.source: Another alternative is to generate static HTML files (just like other static site generators such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__MkDocs__TRILIUM_PH_1__). Since the normal HTML ZIP export does not contain any styling or additional functionality, Trilium provides a way to export the same layout and style as the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Sharing__TRILIUM_PH_3__ function into static HTML files.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing

units.source: Apart from the enhanced security, these HTML files are also easy to deploy on “serverless” deployments such as GitHub Pages or CloudFlare Pages and cache very easily.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing

units.source: Trilium's documentation, available at __TRILIUM_PH_0__docs.triliumnotes.org__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is built using this function of exporting to static HTML files which are then deployed automatically to CloudFlare Pages.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing

units.source: The process is __TRILIUM_PH_0__automated__TRILIUM_PH_1__ by importing the Markdown documentation and exporting it via a script to the static web format.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing

units.source: Differences from normal sharing__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Differences from normal sharing

units.source: Apart from normal __TRILIUM_PH_0__Sharing__TRILIUM_PH_1__, exporting to static HTML files comes with a few subtle differences:
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Differences from normal sharing

units.source: The URL structure is different. Where in normal sharing it's something along the way of __TRILIUM_PH_0__, the notes follow an hierarchical structure, such as __TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Differences from normal sharing

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ is not handled automatically, it needs to be manually added on the server after the export is generated.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Differences from normal sharing

units.source: The “Last updated” for notes is not available.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Differences from normal sharing

units.source: The search functionality works slightly different since the normal one requires an active API to work. In the static export, search still works but uses a different mechanism so results might be different.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Differences from normal sharing

units.source: Differences from normal .zip export__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Differences from normal .zip export

units.source: The name of the files/URLs will prefer __TRILIUM_PH_0__ to allow for clean URLs.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Differences from normal .zip export

units.source: The export requires a functional web server as the pages will not render properly if accessed locally via a web browser due to the use of module scripts.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Differences from normal .zip export

units.source: The directory structure is also slightly different:
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Differences from normal .zip export

units.source: A normal HTML export results in an index file and a single directory.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Differences from normal .zip export

units.source: Instead, for static exporting the top-root level becomes the index file and the child directories are on the root instead.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Differences from normal .zip export

units.source: This makes it possible to easily publish to a website, without forcing everything but the root note to be in a sub-directory.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Differences from normal .zip export

units.source: Testing locally__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Testing locally

units.source: As mentioned previously, the exported static pages require a website to function. In order to test locally, a web server needs to be used.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Testing locally

units.source: One example is to use the Node.js-based __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1____TRILIUM_PH_2__ which can be installed via:
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Testing locally

units.source: Once installed simply:
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Testing locally

units.source: Extract the exported .zip file.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Testing locally

units.source: Inside the extracted directory, run __TRILIUM_PH_0__.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Testing locally

units.source: Access the indicated address (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_0__http://localhost:8080__TRILIUM_PH_1__).
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Testing locally

units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing > Automation
